issues: Dolphin is rendered as a sparse particle/dot scatter cloud rather than a solid lit-phosphor silhouette; it reads like a point-cloud or scatter plot, not a glowing creature.
Dolphin lacks clearly defined anatomy: dorsal fin, pectoral fin, and tail fluke are vague blobs of dots with no crisp outline or rim light.
Dolphin does not dominate; its low dot-density and moderate brightness let the top text and bottom readouts compete for attention.
Anachronistic modern DJ metadata ('133BPM 8A', 'PHR 11/32', 'MIX 0:00 AT 6%') breaks 1998-2003 Pioneer OEL authenticity.
A noisy dotted particle field surrounds and sits below the dolphin, cluttering the mid/lower zone and muddying the water-surface lines.
No visible phosphor body fill or gentle glow halo on the dolphin; objects look like discrete LED dots instead of a continuous OEL phosphor object.
No perceptible short persistence/afterglow trails behind the dolphin, so the motion character of the original is missing.
suggestions: Replace the particle-cloud dolphin with a filled, lit-phosphor silhouette: solid body, crisp outline, distinct dorsal fin, pectoral fin, tail fluke, and a brighter rim-light edge.
Raise dolphin brightness and scale so it occupies ~55% of display height and is unmistakably the first thing the eye lands on.
Remove all anachronistic DJ text (BPM/PHR/MIX); keep only the 3x5 bitmap artist/title line at the top to match the period UI.
Eliminate the random dot-noise field; render water as 2-3 clean, low-contrast horizontal surface lines occupying <=15% height.
Add a subtle phosphor bloom halo (crisp core + soft glow) and a short, clean persistence trail behind the dolphin to evoke real OEL persistence without fog.
Tune the bottom FFT bar graph to a faint, low-contrast row and keep the L/R VU segments small in the bottom-left so the hierarchy dolphin->text->waves->FFT holds.
